slides.body: Joking about NNN makes failing feel harmless. If you're laughing because you couldn't last a week without p*rn — that's not funny. That's a warning.

slides.body: Not "can I win a challenge?" But "why can't I go 11 days without p*rn?" That question is worth answering.

slides.title: Take it [[seriously]]
slides.body: Use November as a real reset — not a meme you quit by day 3. Write down why you're doing it. Make it count.

carousels.name: 8 signs you're using p*rn to escape your life

slides.title: You're not addicted to p*rn. [[You're addicted to escaping your life.]]
slides.sub: 8 signs p*rn is your exit door.

slides.title: Signs [[1–4]]
items: You open p*rn right after a stressful call or message.
You watch p*rn instead of starting the work you're avoiding.
You use it when you feel rejected or not good enough.
Weekends with no plans = more p*rn.

slides.title: Signs [[5–8]]
items: Loneliness hits and p*rn is the first thing you reach for.
You feel nothing after — but you go back anyway.
Your goals keep slipping while p*rn hours stay the same.
You can't sit with silence for 10 minutes.

slides.title: Fix the [[life]], not just the screen
slides.body: Blocking p*rn matters. But if your life feels like something to escape, the urge will find a way back. Build a life you don't want to escape from.

slides.title: Start [[here]]
items: Name what you're escaping — work, loneliness, stress.
Fix one thing about it this week.
Replace p*rn with something that builds you.
Get help if the thing you're escaping is heavy.
slides.note: What does p*rn help you escape? Be honest 👇
